privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.s1.title: The short version
privacy.s1.body: {site} runs in your browser. Your screenshots, projects and exported images are processed on your device and are never uploaded to our servers. We have no accounts and no database.
privacy.s2.title: What stays on your device
privacy.s2.body: Your projects (including uploaded screenshots and settings) are saved in your browser's local storage and IndexedDB so your work survives a refresh. We also store your theme and language preferences. This data never leaves your device, and you can remove it any time by deleting projects in the app or clearing your browser's site data.
privacy.s3.title: Information you send us
privacy.s3.body: If you use the <contact>contact form</contact>, we receive the name, email address and message you type. It is delivered to us by email through EmailJS, a third-party email delivery service, and is used only to respond to you. We don't store it in any database of our own.
privacy.s4.title: Cookies, analytics and tracking
privacy.s4.body: We don't use advertising cookies, analytics or tracking scripts.
privacy.s5.title: Third parties
privacy.s5.body: The site is served by our hosting provider, which may keep standard server logs (such as IP address and user agent) for security and operations. EmailJS processes contact-form messages under its own privacy policy.
privacy.s6.title: Your rights
privacy.s6.body: Since we hold no account data, there is little to access or delete. To ask us to delete an email you sent, or with any privacy question, use the <contact>contact form</contact>.
privacy.s7.title: Children
privacy.s7.body: {site} is not directed at children under 13, and we don't knowingly collect their data.
privacy.s8.title: Changes
privacy.s8.body: We may update this policy; the date above shows the latest revision.
terms.title: Terms of Service
terms.s1.title: Acceptance
terms.s1.body: By using {site} you agree to these terms. If you don't agree, please don't use the app.
terms.s2.title: The service
terms.s2.body: {site} lets you turn screenshots into store-ready marketing images in your browser. We may change, suspend or discontinue features at any time.
terms.s3.title: Your content
terms.s3.body: You keep all rights to the screenshots and images you use and create. You are responsible for having the right to use them, and you must not use the app for unlawful or infringing content. Because your work is stored only in your browser, you are responsible for backing up anything important by exporting it.
terms.s4.title: Acceptable use
terms.s4.body: Don't misuse the service, attempt to disrupt it, or send spam or abusive messages through the contact form.
terms.s5.title: No warranty
terms.s5.body: The service is provided “as is” without warranties of any kind. We don't guarantee it will be uninterrupted or error-free.
terms.s6.title: Limitation of liability
terms.s6.body: To the fullest extent permitted by law, we are not liable for any indirect or consequential damages, or for lost data, arising from your use of the service.

post.app-store-screenshot-sizes.title: App Store and Google Play Screenshot Sizes: A Practical Guide
post.app-store-screenshot-sizes.descript: The screenshot dimensions and counts you need for the App Store and Google Play, and how to export every size from one design.
post.app-store-screenshot-sizes.s0.p0: Both stores reject or distort screenshots that don't match their required dimensions. Each device class has its own size, so a single design usually has to be exported several times.
post.app-store-screenshot-sizes.s0.p1: Store requirements change over time, so treat the numbers below as a starting point and confirm them in App Store Connect and the Google Play Console before you submit.
post.app-store-screenshot-sizes.s1.p0: Apple lets you upload up to 10 screenshots per device size. Larger sizes are scaled down for smaller devices when you don't provide them, so start with the largest iPhone size.
post.app-store-screenshot-sizes.s2.p0: Google Play accepts 2 to 8 phone screenshots. Each side must be between 320 and 3840 px, and the longer side can be at most twice the shorter side. You also need a 1024 × 500 px feature graphic for your listing.
post.app-store-screenshot-sizes.s3.headi: Export every size from one design
post.app-store-screenshot-sizes.s3.p0: Design once, then export to each target. Mockup Studio lets you pick store presets or add custom sizes, then exports all of them together as a ZIP, entirely in your browser.
post.app-screenshot-design-tips.title: 7 Tips for App Store Screenshots That Convert
post.app-screenshot-design-tips.descript: Simple design rules for app store screenshots: clear headlines, one idea per slide, readable text and consistent styling.
post.app-screenshot-design-tips.s0.headi: Your screenshots are your sales pitch
post.app-screenshot-design-tips.s0.p0: Most people decide whether to install an app after glancing at the first few screenshots. They need to understand what the app does within seconds.
post.app-screenshot-design-tips.s1.p0: These habits show up again and again in screenshot sets that perform well:
post.app-screenshot-design-tips.s1.l0: Lead with your strongest benefit in the first slide.
post.app-screenshot-design-tips.s1.l1: Use one idea and one short headline per slide.
post.app-screenshot-design-tips.s1.l2: Keep headline text large enough to read at thumbnail size.
post.app-screenshot-design-tips.s1.l3: Show the real interface, not an abstract illustration.
post.app-screenshot-design-tips.s1.l4: Keep colors, fonts and layout consistent across the whole set.
post.app-screenshot-design-tips.s1.l5: Make sure text has strong contrast against the background.
post.app-screenshot-design-tips.s1.l6: Localize headlines for your biggest markets.
post.app-screenshot-design-tips.s2.p0: Pick a template once and apply it to every screenshot so your set stays consistent. Mockup Studio shows a live preview as you edit headlines, colors and fonts.
post.private-screenshot-mockups-in-brows: Why Browser-Based Screenshot Tools Keep Your App Private
Unreleased app screens are sensitive. Here is why a tool that works entirely in your browser is safer than uploading them.
Screenshots of a pre-launch app can reveal features, branding and plans. Uploading them to a third-party server means trusting that service with that information.
A tool that runs in your browser processes images on your own device. Your files are not sent to a server, so there is nothing to leak, retain or delete later.
Mockup Studio works this way. Your projects are stored locally in your browser and exports are generated on your device. Read our privacy policy for the details.
